newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU says deplores Serb crackdown on radio stations.
newsitem.headline: EU says deplores Serb crackdown on radio stations.

text.p: The European Union on Wednesday deplored Serbia's crackdown on independent radio stations and expressed dismay that the authorities there had ignored international calls to observe democratic principles.

"The EU deplores the decision of the federal authorities on December 3 to declare Radio B-92 illegal and to prevent it and another independent radio station, Radio Index from broadcasting," Ireland, current holder of the rotating EU presidency, said in a statement on behalf of the 15-nation bloc.

"It notes with dismay that the Serb authorities seem determined to ignore calls from the international community... for the full observance of international democratic principles," the statement said.
The EU's External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek expressed "dismay" in a separate statement at the news that the Serb authorities had declared Radio B-92 illegal.
"Mr van den Broek deplores this decision which is not compatible with the need for guaranteeing freedom of expression, including free media," the statement issued in Brussels said.
"The Commissioner urges the Belgrade authorities to restore Radio B-92 to the airwaves immediately and allow it to broadcast freely, and to cease exerting pressure against other media."
Serbia cracked down on the radio stations to halt their live reports of daily opposition demonstrations against President Slobodan Milosevic.
The demonstrations began after the authorities annulled an opposition victory in local polls held on November 17. Milosevic has threatened use of force to quell the protests.
Radio B-92 said its transmitter was switched off on Tuesday and the communications ministry ordered it to stop broadcasting while the student Radio Index was also knocked off the air.
"The EU considers it essential that independent democratic voices are allowed to be heard. It calls on the authorities to reverse their decision," the statement issued in Dublin added.
The EU said it had been following the situation with "grave concern".

"The EU will continue to monitor closely the situation the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and reiterates its call for all sides to exercise restraint at this time of heightened political tension," it said.
